name: Knead-Away

card.summary: A vintage Sears massager sold for body contouring, used by rubbing or kneading problem areas in the hope of a slimmer-looking shape.
card.note: Mid-century slimming gadgets are collectibles; no studies of this model exist.

quick.overview:
Knead-Away is a vintage Sears massager, described in collector listings as a slimming device. Like other mid-century home massagers, it is used on the body to knead areas people want to look slimmer.

The appearance payoff users hope for is a smoother, slimmer contour. No published studies of this specific product are known.
quick.how: Users apply the device to the body, typically over thighs, hips or abdomen, in a routine. Exact usage depends on the original instructions that came with it.
quick.risks: Vigorous massage can bruise or irritate skin. Vintage electric appliances may have aged wiring.

lead: Knead-Away is a vintage Sears massager sold as a slimming device. People use this kind of home massager by working it over the thighs, hips, abdomen or other areas they want to look smoother and slimmer, hoping for a more contoured silhouette.

It belongs to the mid-twentieth-century family of electric home massagers, roller machines and vibrating belts that were sold with promises of reshaping the body. Today it turns up mainly in collector and resale listings, often with its box and instruction booklet.

angle.text: The device is described as a slimming massager; the contour change is the claim made for this type of product.

paras: Knead-Away is listed by collectors as a Sears-branded massager marketed for body contouring. Like other appliances of its period, it is a mains-powered gadget meant for use at home, with the kneading or vibrating action applied directly to the skin or over light clothing.

The intended use is localised: the device is held or positioned over a problem area and moved around in sessions, with the stated aim of a slimmer-looking shape. As with other slimming massagers of its era, the contour change is the claim made for the product, and users typically describe it as part of a regular routine.
Vigorous massage can leave temporary redness or bruising. Vintage electric appliances can have aged cords and insulation, and collectors often sell them as display pieces or working vintage items.
